task_instance: Triage a recurring MCP connector OAuth failure (works, then 401s once per day, re-auth fixes it until next day) by collecting a redacted token record and an ordered connector event log, then running the skill's classifier scripts/oauth_triage.py to get a machine-readable fault-class verdict and next probe.
blocker_detail: The skill's core deliverable is the verdict produced by running its bundled Python classifier (scripts/oauth_triage.py) over the token record and connector log. This office-assistant runtime cannot run code, scripts, or shell commands of any kind, so the classifier cannot be executed and no verdict (primary_class, confidence, findings, next_probe, exit code) can be produced. Per the run rules I did not write my own replacement, stub, or fabricate the classifier's output. The script and its reference files are present next to SKILL.md, so this is not a missing-skill-file problem; the missing ability is code execution.
evidence: Read the skill at engineering/skills/mcp-oauth-triage/SKILL.md; its Usage/Workflow require 'python3 scripts/oauth_triage.py --token-file ./token.json --log ./connector.jsonl --json'. Confirmed via Glob that scripts/oauth_triage.py and scripts/run_fixtures.py plus assets/fixtures and expected_outputs/verdicts.json all exist in the skill tree (so the deliverable depends on executing them, not on a missing file). Prepared realistic input a user would supply inside the work directory: token.json (a nested-envelope token record with a relative expires_in and a refresh_token length marker) and connector.jsonl (ordered exchange/store/load/call events showing two exchanges within the same second and a 401 after refresh). Attempting the deliverable requires invoking the Python interpreter on these inputs, which the runtime does not permit; no other granted tool (text read/write/edit) can execute the classifier, so the verdict could not be produced or verified.
